description:
FILED s415, found by the #371 work.

`CORE::state $x = â¦` was NOT being normalised to `state $x = â¦`, because the
source-level pass that strips the CORE:: prefix shares the `($str_re)|`
pass-through that any quote imbalance defeats (see the s415 DECIDED entry).
With that fixed, two companion files now REACH the v2 state gates and die
where they used to transpile:

  t/op/sub.t           C 52/13  -> TRANSPILE-FAIL
      "Parser2 TODO: state $x in named sub (string eval)"
      (t/op/sub.t's CORE::state inside a string eval; perl-tests/sub.t's own
       CORE::state at line 244 is in a supported position and lowers natively)
  t/opbasic/concat.t   C 248/6  -> TRANSPILE-FAIL
      "Parser2 TODO: state $y rewrite (my re-declaration of $y in scope)"
      line 203:  ok(ref(CORE::state $y = "a $o b") eq 'o', â¦)

THIS IS NOT A REGRESSION TO REVERT.  Before the fix, `CORE::state $x = 42`
lowered as a plain PACKAGE ASSIGNMENT (`(p-scalar-= $x 42)`) â a state
declaration silently compiled to something else, the #138 failure class the
project treats as the worst.  The rows those two files still passed were
passing on a program PCL had mis-parsed.  The loud `Parser2 TODO:` die is the
correct answer until the two shapes are implemented.

WHAT TO IMPLEMENT (Pl/Parser2.pm, _state_rewrite_routes / _state_rw_blocker,
around line 5340):
  1. a `state` declaration whose name is re-declared with `my` later in the
     same scope â the rewrite renames the declaration and its uses, and stops
     at the sibling redeclaration (the #296-B2 rule already states how);
  2. `state` in a named sub compiled inside a string eval â the eval-mode
     route needs the per-sub cell the file-mode route builds.
Recovering both files is the acceptance measure (52 + 248 companion rows), plus
a Pl/t row per shape probed against perl.

Related: the state family's other gates (#337), and docs/not-supported.md has
no `state` section â write one if these stay unimplemented past v0.1.

HALF DONE s415 (commit s415e): t/opbasic/concat.t RECOVERED (248 rows), t/op/sub.t
still blocked.

WHAT WAS OBSOLETE, and is now gone:
  * the expression route's `_state_rw_blocker` refusal on ANY my/our/local
    re-declaration of the name in the root, and
  * the named-sub route's "multiple declarations" refusal (its caller simply
    never passed the `shadow_ok` waiver its own blocker already had).
Both existed because a positional rename of every `$y` in the root would merge
two variables -- but `_rename_decl_within` has been SHADOW-AWARE since #254
B-ii and region-limited since #296-B2: it starts at the state declaration,
leaves an inner re-declaration's own scope alone, and stops at a LATER
declaration of the same name.  Probed against perl 5.40.3 in all three
orderings (inner `my` in a nested block; a later `my` at the same level; a
`my` BEFORE the state decl, which the state decl shadows from its own point
on) -- identical, and the three are guard rows 34-36 in Pl/t/state-01.t.
Bar: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files, gate 151/5562, full sweep GATE
clean TOTAL 18369 (+0) -- and the sweep IS the gate for a rename change.

WHAT REMAINS (t/op/sub.t, 52 rows): `_shadow_rename_blocker`'s STRING-EVAL
refusal, which is real, not obsolete.  A string eval inside the sub captures
lexicals BY NAME through the site alist (`_eval_lexical_alist`), and a state
rename produces a defvar'd CELL that never enters `_let_bound_vars`, so the
eval would look up `$x` and miss it.  The fix is the same shape as the
span-mangled file cells already handled there: Parser2 publishes an
original -> state-cell map for the scopes in play and ExprToCL appends those
pairs.  TREAT AS ITS OWN TASK: the eval-capture path is where #296's bugs
lived, and there is a trap to answer first -- p-eval caches by source+package,
so a capture-dependent EMISSION must key that cache (memory
`project_one_compiler_state`).  Recovering t/op/sub.t's 52 rows is the measure.

FOUND ON THE WAY: task #402 -- string interpolation stringifies instead of
CONCATENATING, so an overloaded `.` never runs ([perl #124160]).  That is what
concat.t:203 asserts; the row now RUNS and fails honestly (it was failing
before too, for a worse reason).


CLOSED s418c (Fable) â the eval half SHIPPED.  The fix is this task's own
sketch on the M5 block-cell precedent: Parser2 registers original->cell when
the state DECL STATEMENT lowers (_eval_state_captures â visibility starts at
perl's masking point), scoped by _lower_sub's save/restore WITHOUT the
_let_bound_vars wipe (nested subs inherit; the cells are defvars so the
wipe's hazard cannot apply); _eval_lexical_alist appends the pairs after
let-bound (my-shadow wins), before span.  Waived ONLY for a scalar decl at
the top level of the sub's own block; inner-block decls + containers keep
the refusal.  THE CACHE LEG NEEDED NO CODE: #296-B1's key already carries
capture NAMES and the alist VALUE resolves at runtime â probed with two subs
eval'ing the same text (ABA).  t/op/sub.t TRANSPILE-FAIL -> DIFF 53/12, one
row better than the s410 snapshot.  Eight probes vs perl identical.  Guard
Pl/t/state-eval-01.t.  Design record: docs/session-log.md s418 +
docs/DECIDED.md s418c.
subject: Two v2 state gates are now REACHED (CORE::state normalises since s415): t/op/sub.t and t/opbasic/concat.t die instead of mis-lowering a state declaration as a package assignment -- 300 companion rows to recover
